title: Town of Salem
text: Town of Salem is a ton of fun, especially with friends. In Town of Salem you get assigned a role and join a town of, usually, 14 others. There are a huge variety of roles! And even more will be added with an upcoming expansion that looks really promising! These roles are (but not limited to): Mayor, Medium, Investigator, Escort, Consigliere, Amnesiac, Godfather, Executioner, Jester, Serial Killer, and so on. Based on your role you have a distinct goal. The Mafia are supposed to work together to kill all who oppose, the serial killer must finish EVERYONE, and the town must survive to see the end of all evildoers and killers, etc. What's amazing is that despite the fact that there are some 30 roles or so, almost every role feels very distinct and has a unique playstyle (apart from escort/consort which I think are the most boring roles in the game). So one thing Town of Salem does very well is that it makes the gameplay always unique. This is true because there are so many distinct roles, but also because NO GAME of Town of Salem ever plays out the same way. The constant wondering of who is who and whether or not you can trust those who stand to your left and right create such tension that the game is almost always exciting. Even in death you can still possibly affect the outcome by communicating with the medium. In my opinion, this is Town of Salem's greatest strength. Town of Salem also does freemium gaming right (for the most part). There are two types of in-game currencies. One can only be purchased with real world $$$, and the other is earned after each match. Almost all items can be purchased with the in-game currency. There are only a select few which can only be purchased with real $$$, and they are all cosmetic. The only items which aren't purely cosmetic are "Scrolls" and they simply increase the likelihood you get to play a certain role over another. Despite all these positives though, there are some negatives.. Young playerbase The playerbase APPEARS (I'm not sure of this) to be quite young, and some of the logic of the players seems lacking sometimes. However, there are different game modes and by gravitating more towards ranked play you can avoid those who are just goofing off. Night 1 Night 1 honestly sucks because it's very possible to die night 1 and there are many roles in which, if you die the first night or any of the early nights, your presence is essentially useless and the rest of the game is a snorefest. Nightmares about getting killed on night 1 more have honestly woken me up in the middle of the night lol. Random Lynchings This is somewhat tied to the first complaint, but in normal matches and even in ranked play sometimes, townies will randomly lynch people without much rhyme or reason. It's pretty frustrating if you play a critical role and your town randomly lynches you and greatly hurts your chance of victory, or even more frustrating if they somehow make a rally smart choice and you were the serial killer, mafia, executioner, etc. High(ish) learning curve There are A TON of abbreviations players use in the game to make communication fast and effective, since you only have so much time to talk each day. So, for new players, learning all the abbreviations and initialisms can be quite tiring and take a while. I have 10 hours at the same of this review though and by now I am pretty comfortable with all abbreviations, though. So it's not too bad. These, relatively tiny, complaints aside though, Town of Salem is a great game and honesly has provided me with a very fun and never old casual gaming experience. It has brought an even better version to a classic game which I LOVED to play with my friends at gettogethers when I was younger. One final note: You may be thinking "Why do I buy this game on Steam? It's a free broswer game!". That's true. However, one thing to consider is that the new expansion will come out soon, and it will be $10 online, and only $5 if you buy this version on Steam, so either way everyone will have spent $10 altogether. In addition, the game awards currency to be used on cosmetic upgrades for your character. If yoy buy the Steam version you get 100% more in-game currency after every completed match. It's a really nice bonus. All in all, you should get this game. It's fun, it never gets old, the roles are unique, a new expansion is coming, the profanity filter is actually hilarious, and the game is very casual. It's a great fit for almost any type of gamer, because this is a classic we all used to love playing with our friends, made a lot more accesible and easier.

title: Town of Salem
text: A fantastic formula, lacking in polish and refinement. This game has a role system and premise that is immediately enticing to anyone who enjoys mind gaming people, is interested in psychology, or likes reading people's behavior. The task is simple; carry out your role's objective, for the most part staying alive and outing those who would inhibit your survival. Some special roles turn this on its head and require you to get yourself or someone else executed intentionally. The game plays very quickly, decisions have to be snappy and conclusions leapt to, there's no opportunity for overthinking. If you want to win, you need to have a strategy and be ready to evolve that strategy. The learning curve can seem very steep in the first few matches. If you fail to act appropriately, you WILL be letting others on your team down. I don't mind this fact, because even failure can be thoroughly entertaining. The human drama that unfolds with each new match is always unique and you might even suprise yourself with your own actions and decisions. The games you've played will stick with you after you leave your chair. That time you lynched the sherriff. That time you almost got discovered as the serial killer and had to hold back the knife for a night. That perfect lie you told that kept the noose off your neck. The time no one believed you and all died night after night, while you smugly sighed in dead chat. Unfortunately, from a technical perspective there's a LOT that can go wrong here. Lag is a beast, and missing a vote or a night action, or even one line of chat can mean the difference between saving the town and shooting the killer at your door. I've experienced a few crashes, and from what others have said these can get me penalized for 'leaving the game in progress.' There are a multitude of ways people can spoil the fun, although I haven't been able to detect obvious cheating or gamethrowing in the matches I've played. I consider myself fortunate and applaud whatever systems in place for swaying the odds. The interface and graphics are in a state similar to newgrounds flash games from the early 2000's. I don't consider these features part of the main draw of the game, so I don't mind at all. I recieved this game from the Humble Bundle, and haven't yet spent the in-game currency. It seems the best thing you could buy with it would be items that can make roles more likely to be assigned to you. I haven't really felt attached to any particular roles yet, so haven't tried the items. I spent a couple of hours reading the community guides once I felt I was ready to learn more and get better. When it works right, it's extremely enjoyable. This is my first online board game since chess over 10 years ago, so I'm no expert in the genre. My experience was based on unranked matches of the basic non-custom game type. I've played every role but jailor and jester now. I asked a question in the forums and a dev responded within hours. Good stuff.

text: Buggy, yet quite unique take on the tower defense genre. Unfortunately, it left Early Access too soon and seems more-or-less abandoned at this point, as if the devs had decided to prioritize other titles instead. Scumbag move! But if this game works for you and the bugs aren't too distracting, like the lack of music in-game, then it's hard to put down. The units are all awesome, and you can take direct control of ALL of them, and then of some other extra air and ground units at your disposal, so you can take matter on your own hands if things get to hectic, like a F-14 Tomcat, an Apache helicopter, WWI era tanks or the Red Baron's own aircraft just to mention some. From WWI to the Cold War, there's lots of content here and factions, all DLCs for both games are already included, so lots of hours of fun. Quite strategic in its use of units and upgrades, since every upgrade comes with side effects, like longer reloading times for WWI era artillery, or with different effects in the case of modern American artillery -spread instead of direct ammo/howitzer with precise munitions vs barrage of MLRS- or a mortar emplacement with bio-chemical ammo that later can be turned into a flamethrower and then into a regular mortar with napalm effects, each with their own pluses and cons. To add variety to an already varied game, you can make use of random special powers, abilities and you can also take control of a hero, but it's not really necessary, and that's only if you manage to obtain them by killing enemy units directly in a combo. The bosses are awesome, they're these humongous machines that dwarf any other units so they're always fun and interesting to fight. Having said that, I would give this game a neutral rating due to the Early Access blunder and amount of bugs, and the lack of in-game music really pisses me off. But this being Steam, it's either a thumbs down a thumbs up, so I'm going with a positive rating overall since I did indeed enjoy my time with Toy Soldiers: Complete.

text: Played this for over 8k hours. Best game ever. And then Maniaplanet 4 was released. It's a little bit shinier, but a lot of the things that made the original game so fun (imo) have been removed. Bugs that many 'lol' tracks relied on have been 'fixed' and a lot of the old records are now unobtainable. I still reservedly recommend it; it's a good game. But with the update the appeal, for me at least, has been severly hammered. A very sad week; I doubt I'll be playing the new version anywhere near as much. :( (Edit: Now things have stabalised somewhat, I'm still playing a lot.) Original review follows. --------------------------------- Why so much time on what looks like a pretty basic, arcady, and completely unrealistic racing game? Well, after 3k+ hours, there are probably about 3k+ reasons. Let me try and pick a few. First off, this is very much skill-based. Even on the 'silly, luck' tracks (which I'll come to in a moment). Play online, and you'll find pro-level gamers showing almost unbelievable levels of skill and achieving the seemingly impossible. But it's not impossible - this is a very fair game. Any cheating is caught and eliminated pretty quickly. All the cars have the same spec, there is no car-to-car collision to mess up your times. It's (mostly) just you, and a track, and your level of skill that determine how well you do. Next, the variety. The track creator provided allows an almost limitless tracks, and the community has produced masses of content. This obviously varies enormously in both style and quality, but since you are generally only on any given track for 4-5 minutes, if you don't like one you just wait it out and see if the next is more your kind of thing. And probably, in those 4-5 minutes you'll try it anyway and still get sucked in to try and beat your own times at the very least. [continued in comments]

title: Trauma
text: Trauma may seem deceptively simple at first: it's a flash game about exploring the dreams of a girl who's been through an accident. It will probably take 30 min to an hour to finish the main path, yet there are hidden secrets and alternate ways to end a dream. Trauma is all about exploration and is very light on the challenge. It plays like an out of body experience. The main puzzle is navigation through a set of mouse gestures. The girl will narrate the dream logic as she recognizes signs from her real past. Each dream has a core dilemma that needs to be solved. The light gameplay is more than compensated by the depth of story ideas. Through each dream, you start knowing more about the protagonist and by the end, symbols start falling into place. The dreams are interconnected; you will find recurring ideas, and some solutions are applicable in more than one situation. Trauma is best played right before bed. It will make you think about the stuff that goes through your head at night.

text: Trauma is more of an interactive story than a game. The story involves a woman who has been hospitalized and you travel through her dreams through a series of photographs. Navigating your way through the dreams takes some practice but you learn as you travel through the different dreams and then it becomes easy. The dreams themselves can be trippy and it is cool to see certain interactions with objects. The reason that I cannot recommend Trauma is that there is nothing to drive you to play the game. The story is extremely vague. You don't know exactly why you are traveling through these dreams or what they mean. Almost nothing is revealed about the main character; only vagued ideas about how she is feeling. The game is also very short. Alternate objectives can be completed but with no story to provide a driving force, you don't really want to be a completionist. It's not a bad attempt for an indie project but it just needs a bit more of everything to keep it from falling into obscurity.

title: Trauma
text: TRAUMA is one of those games where you can't really call it a "Game" since there's no actual gameplay. It's more like an interactive short film about someone's psyche. It reminded me a lot of Dear Esther, which I also recommended. TRAUMA is a point and click game where you discover the meaning of this woman's dreams, and event's in her life that may impact her dream. It does it's job well, as all four locations feel like a lucid dream. Keep in mind this game is definitely not for everyone. It's not a point-and-click adventure game in the since of The Walking Dead or Sam and Max. Most hardcore gamers would probably be turned off at the lack of gameplay and deviation from the norm of most modern games. Even the story itself is pretty vague, most of it is left to the player's interpretation. But it's uniqueness is what I liked about this. If you're looking for something to wrap your brain around, or are just looking for something different I'd say give this one a try.

title: Trauma
text: Trauma is a very artsy puzzle-adventure kind of game. Graphics 6 of 10 The graphics consist mainly of photo-shots of urban everyday areas. I’d say they're okayish. For an indie game developer that's ok. Still feels old school. Gameplay 5 of 10 You navigate through the photo-shots and you manipulate various objects with gestures /signs. Think of the swiping movements you do with your fingers on a smartphone...but here you do it with a mouse. Which is in no way intuitive or comfortable. It’s meant to be an adventure game, but it's not very adventurous to me. The areas where you are allowed to do something are sparse. And so you click your way through the artsy still photo-shots...while a tragic little story unfolds. On the plus side the atmosphere is quite nice and feels dreamlike and obscure at times. Sound 6 of 10 The voice of the actress is quite well done. Music is almost nonexistent. Final verdict I would not recommend this game. Although it has its moments and the story is bittersweet, the gameplay just doesn't feel right, the puzzles are way too easy and it's extremely short and can be accomplished in like 45 minutes

title: Trauma
text: This game has very mixed reviews for a reason. From the description I expected it to be a point and click adventure game. In reality it is more like something you would find as an interactive media installation in a gallery for contemporary art. As a matter of fact it's a project created by german design students. The game let's you experience several surreal dream scenes entirely composed of heavily manipulated photographs. In each of this scenes you can find hidden memory fragments and have to solve gesture based puzzle. There a are also some short videos and spoken dialogue (with strong german accent). You can play through the game in less than an hour. So if you are expecting a full-fledged adventure game you will be disappointed (especially for the steep price). Despite all of that I still enjoyed the game and would recommend checking it out. But only if you are really into contemporary multimedia art or can get it for cheap.

title: Trauma
text: With a pretentious "Fin" at the end, the author wanted to make sure you understand that this not just a game, it's a piece of art. Get it? Anyway, other than that, it was an interesting experience. Played late at night with the lights off, the game manages to create an eerie, sometimes creepy atmosphere. The voice acting is good and contributes substantially to the mood of the game. While this is essentially a point-and-click game, it is unlike any other I’ve seen. It introduces several original gameplay elements that make it stand out from the crowd. While the game has a "Fin", it doesn’t quite seem to have an ending, at least not a particularly meaningful one. One could easily end up asking himself, "ok, but what was the point of all that?" I suppose that it is more about the journey, not the destination, and the author’s focus was more on style over substance, but in the end, this could have been a much better game if it actually had a more meaningful story and conclusion. Worth buying when on sale.

title: Trauma
text: Short, artsy puzzle game with a unique premise $7 may be pushing the pice/value ratio, get it on discount The main characer was in an accident (hence the title "Trauma"). The locations are still scenes with cutscene animations. The game is told by finding photographs which you try to match with scenes that are visible. There are 4 separate "adventures" (chapters?), each with a primary and 3 alternate endings, but the photographs relate to things anong the different chapters. You can complete these in any order, and it helps sometimes to bounce around since you will find hints related to different chapters. You win the game by finding the primary ending in all 4 chapters, and this can be done in less than an hour. The real way to play is to look for all 9 photographs and unlock all alternate endings in all the chapters - this might take 2-3 hours. The setting is present day with surrealist aspects. In addition to cutscene animations, there are short live action videos at the beginning and end of the game, and after you solve each chapter. You navigate between one still scene location and another by either moving to an adjacent location (visible when you mouse to the edge of the location) or you can jump to a limited extent by drawing gestures on the screen. The puzzle part of the game is discovering which gestures work and which locations you need to use them. The music and voice acting is unremarkable, I actually play with the sounds off since I got tired of the "Doesn't work" sound when I use a wrong gesture. The display resolution is less than HD, but it didn't really affect anything. To sum up, if you want an artsy experience with intresting visuals for a few hours, then get this game, but at 50% or better discount.

title: Trauma
text: An incredibly short and sad game, point and click but very user friendly with a low learning curve. Less of a game and more of a vignette about the protagonist. Charitably you could put this down to the fact the protagonist is having these flashbacks/hallucinations, but it breaks the flow and feel of the game - in my opinion. If the voice acting was better I would recommend this to everyone, but as is i'd only recommend it if you're going to pick it up during a Steam sale, as I did, for $1.75. It's worth that, and maybe next time the Devs' next project will be a bigger success. Gets points for effort and originality of concept though.

title: Tree of Savior (English Ver.)
text: You know I was thinking about actually sitting down and getting to the end game of this game. Everytime I do it, the same problems arise. I have picked up Tree of savior over and over. Not three times, not four. Think this is my sixth time picking it up? At first I felt like the combat rework was nice, in its own way with a bunch of other benefits to it, with some drawbacks but still. Its not a bad update if you like this type of game I guess. Overall, I won't recommend the game to anyone for a number of reasons. I won't be listing everything, but I will be listing a lot of flak the game has with me personally and honestly. Not sure why i keep picking it back up. I actually do know, and its the only game me and my friend can pick up and play for a bit, other than that we just play overwatch here and there. Honestly I don't really enjoy overwatch, but its funny at times which honestly makes it good enough. Well, time to list stuff I guess. POSITIVES: - Art style - EXP card system - Class/rank system NEGATIVES: - Questing/leveling system - meh story, be the judge on that. feels like a generic story to me, but then again all mmos USUALLY fall into this category. - Progression. This is somewhat to do with the leveling system. It feels worse as you go depending on the class you are. Yes, there is better builds out there. but solo leveling is a nightmare. I've been left to solo level here and there, and it gets worse. If I'm gonna be bothered to do end game. I don't want to sit there 4000 years just progressing without doing a certain way. There is ways to level properly, then theres questing. Its just a pain honestly. Its better than it used to be. - The grind, has felt worse than any game ever. I've played Black Desert, and that games grind is acceptable in comparison to me. - Combat system. IF you like tab target games, fine. Whatever. I don't care really. but I will say this. Why make a "middle ground" That sucks in general, and feels misleading straight up? "What?" You might be asking? Well. Heres the thing. If the middle ground worked in the first place, I think those games would be much better off than the seperate 'genres'. However, they're not. They bring this middle ground that sucks for the "action" players. Dodging AoE's, and so on is NOT action combat. Examples of what people seem to think action combat is; Guild Wars 2, Blade and soul, Revelation Online, Tree of savior. Think you might get the gist here. I'm also NOT saying that its advertising this, I'm critiquing the fact that it went the middle ground route that just makes it feel bad to play. I'm also critiquing this in general because I'm absolutely sick and tired of people spewing and claiming stupid things. A middle ground isn't the way to go. It feels bad on both ends, even if its tab with more action, it still feels tab. And if you make others play 'action' but others play tab, or deal with tab stuff. It feels bad, being pelted with spells from a distance that auto lock on, no matter how far you run as long as it was casted in set range, while I'm stuck in an 'action' based system. - The cash shop feels unbelievably expensive and overpriced. I don't think there anything worth the price, but maybe if you like it you'll splurge on it. Although I'd rather just burn my money personally. CONCLUSION:  Honestly, I've tried repeatedly. I've tried other games over and over. Its just another MMORPG I've tried to love, with its only redeemable thing for me is the class/rank and art style. Its probably better than it was for actual players who enjoy this. For me. I'm just gonna do the massive pass. Hopefully I can just find a game me and my friend enjoy. For now I'll just go back to staring at my monitor, being depressed and wishing for another mmo I can waste my life on. Or just.. stare at my monitor more until my mother kicks me out. Whichever works.
